confidence_notes: I ran 5 web searches on food and drink prices plus 1 for the RBA rate. Cappuccino (about 70 MXN, roughly US$4) and draft beer (a 2026 aggregator average of about 52 MXN for 0.5 L, roughly US$3) have reasonable support from aggregator and travel-blog figures. Meal prices vary widely between Tulum town and the beach/hotel zone. The inexpensive meal is a town-based estimate of about 150 MXN for lunch, plus other guides. The mid-range meal for two is a bounded estimate from a Numbeo-derived figure of about US$58 (undated), a town-restaurant guide of US$10-20 per person and a beach-zone range that is much higher. I found no direct 2026 cocktail price for town. The cocktail is estimated from blog ranges (about US$9 downtown, US$10-15 at beach hotels) and a roughly 2.5-3x multiple of beer. Wine by the glass rests mainly on one chain restaurant's menu (about 175 MXN, roughly US$10), tempered toward town prices, so it is weak. MXN-to-USD conversions are approximate and used the pairings given in the sources. Accommodation anchors are holistic model estimates from general knowledge of Tulum town and its demand, not live listings, and are the least certain anchors. Tulum is expensive for Mexico and prices vary a lot by zone and season, with July near low season. The RBA observation is the latest I found on the generation date (2026-11-19). The user's pricing window is July 2026.
comparable_city_reasoning: Tulum is priced above the Mexican average and closer to Playa del Carmen and Cancun's tourist zones than to Mexico City. Town (pueblo) prices set the restaurant and drink anchors, with some upward weighting for beach-zone tourist pricing. Accommodation reflects Riviera Maya coast demand.
